facts.text: Highland was founded in December 1858 by land promoter William Larimer Jr., who also founded Denver City the month before.
Highland sits in Denver’s city‑center, bounded by West 38th Avenue north, a Union Pacific line east, the South Platte River southeast, Speer Boulevard south, and Federal Boulevard west.
Within the Highlands, historic designations include Potter Highlands, Scottish Highlands, and Highlands Park, each reflecting different eras of the neighborhood.
Potter Highlands is celebrated for its deep roots in Denver’s early settlement, drawing visitors to its storied streets and historic homes.
A 1½‑hour walking tour guides guests through Potter Highlands, highlighting its oldest neighborhood status and the stories of its founding families.
In 1859 the Highland town company formed, planning a Platte River bridge to connect the new town with Auraria and Denver.
